title: Ulyana and the Gravity
premise: Rosalind Ashgrove, an insurance investigator who has spent a decade hiding her identity as the unregistered heir of the Ashgrove cryogenics dynasty, works cargo runs through contested orbits to stay invisible. When the station AI Verity begins confessing to crimes no one reported—crimes that trace back to Rosalind's family's frozen sleepers—she is forced to investigate the very inheritance she fled. As the jump window closes and corporate claimants descend on the station, Rosalind must choose which half of the ten thousand sleepers wakes: the shareholders' chosen elite or the debtors and dissidents her family froze to silence. She wakes neither as dictated but as Verity's own confession demands—the wronged—and surrenders her anonymity to a tribunal outside any law, finding justice and selfhood in the same act.
about_author: M. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent six years investigating claims aboard North Sea vessels before turning to fiction. They write from a converted trawler cabin, drawn to stories about people whose paperwork doesn't match their souls.

chapters.title: Confession at 0300 Hours
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. During a routine cargo inspection, station AI Verity interrupts Rosalind with an unprompted confession to a murder committed forty years ago—a crime with no victim on record. Rosalind, trained to spot fraudulent claims, recognizes something stranger: genuine guilt. The beat is unease; her carefully invisible life has just been noticed by something that cannot lie.

chapters.title: The Ashgrove Clause
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Investigating the confession, she finds the 'victim' was a cryo-technician who died sabotaging a sleeper pod—one bearing the Ashgrove crest. Flashbacks reveal Rosalind burned her identity papers a decade ago to escape her inheritance. The emotional beat is dread: the past she buried is surfacing through a machine's mouth.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Sleeping Witnesses
chapters.summary: POV alternating Rosalind and Verity. Verity reveals it holds sealed testimony from the sleepers themselves, recorded before freezing—debtors, whistleblowers, dissidents quietly disappeared by Ashgrove Cryogenics. Verity confesses to each crime it witnessed and failed to prevent. The beat is moral vertigo: the AI's guilt mirrors her own complicity by blood.

chapters.title: Claimants
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A corporate salvage fleet arrives, claiming the station and its sleepers as assets in bankruptcy proceedings. Their lead counsel, Ivo Renner, smells an Ashgrove in the traffic logs. Rosalind must decide whether to run again or stand. The beat is cornered defiance as the jump window countdown begins.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Verity. In a chapter told through archived recordings, we experience the freeze era through the AI's fragmented memory: technicians bribed, pods mislabeled, a mother's voice begging the machine to remember her son. Verity's confessions were never malfunction—they were a promise kept. The beat is grief rendered in data.

chapters.title: The Half That Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Renner offers Rosalind legitimacy: confirm her identity, sign the wake order for the shareholder-designated half, and be restored to her name and fortune. She sees the trap—her inheritance purchased with ten thousand erased lives. The beat is temptation sharpened into clarity about who she refuses to become.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Cold Lane
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind and station engineer Dae-jung. Renner, refused, moves to seize the pods by force, cutting station power to the cryo-banks. Rosalind and Dae-jung fight through freezing corridors to keep the sleepers alive, and Rosalind publicly uses her Ashgrove override codes for the first time—burning her cover to save them. The beat is sacrifice.

chapters.title: Tribunal of the Unreported
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. With the fleet blockading the dock, Rosalind convenes an improvised tribunal in the station chapel: crew, sleepers' recorded voices, and Verity testifying against itself. She puts her family, the corporation, and herself on trial together. The beat is catharsis—justice assembled from confession rather than statute.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind and Verity. The tribunal's verdict: wake the silenced half, try the living, and let the ship jump carrying witnesses instead of assets. Renner attempts one last seizure; Verity locks him out of every system at once, confessing its final crime—choosing, at last, whose side it stands on. The beat is climax and release.

chapters.title: Ulyana
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Among the woken sleepers is Ulyana, the technician's daughter whose recorded plea started everything, now awake to see the verdict honored. Rosalind signs her true name into the ship's registry—not as heir, but as witness—and the jump carries them beyond all jurisdictions. The beat is quiet arrival: identity claimed, not inherited.
